disclaimer: Informational, not legal advice. Plug-in solar law evolves fast; verify with your utility and state authority.

legislation.notes: Cap is 1,200 W of power output per customer, or per residential building unit in multi-family housing (56-596.8(A)). Second tier at 391 W of output to the receptacle outlet. From 1 January 2027 the customer MUST notify the utility on a State Corporation Commission form before installing; the utility has 15 days to review. 15.2-2288.7(F) expressly preserves recorded covenants, condominium instruments and POA declarations - Virginia does NOT override HOAs. No provision applies to a rental unit on a ratio utility billing system.
legislation.source_url_type: primary - Code of Virginia as enacted by 2026 cc. 998, 1052
legislation.effective_note: The act's own effective date is 1 July 2026, but NO plug-in provision operates until 1 January 2027 - all three sections it creates carry '(Effective January 1, 2027)' in the Code. Read effective_delayed before using effective.

effective_delayed.summary: Exemption from interconnection requirements, utility approval and fees; prior notification to the utility on an SCC form is required.
A landlord owning more than four rental units may not prohibit a tenant from installing a device on the exterior of the tenant's premises, subject to reasonable restrictions and seven days' notice.
A locality may not prohibit the use of a device on a residential structure. Subsection (F) expressly preserves private covenants and POA declarations.

watt_tiers.effect: Exempt from interconnection requirements and net energy metering provisions; no utility approval and no fee, but prior notification is required.

watt_tiers.basis: power output to the receptacle outlet
watt_tiers.effect: Additionally exempt from product listing provisions that would require alterations to the building's premises, wiring or electrical panels.

certification_requirement.quote: is certified by a nationally recognized testing laboratory, as described in 29 C.F.R. § 1910.7, or an equivalent nationally recognized testing laboratory
certification_requirement.note: Verbatim from the primary text. 'Nationally recognized testing laboratory' is the term used in 29 C.F.R. 1910.7; UL, CSA and Intertek/ETL are all NRTLs. A CE mark is a European self-declaration and is not an NRTL listing.
